subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core `messages.operationalReplies` policy that can silence or redirect runtime operational notices, and what security/product proof is required before that becomes a public config and plugin-hook contract?
rationale: This cannot be decided mechanically because the PR intentionally changes privacy-sensitive source-chat delivery behavior, adds a new operator config surface, and touches a security-owned dependency surface.

options.title: Require Security/Product Review Before Merge
options.body: Keep the PR open but require the shrinkwrap to be removed or explicitly authorized, the branch rebased, the config/API contract approved, and real affected-channel proof added before merge.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Bug Fixes
options.body: Ask for narrower PRs that fix specific notice leaks with existing `visibleReplies` and `suppressToolErrors` behavior before adding a general policy knob.

options.title: Reject The Core Config Surface
options.body: Close or redirect the broad policy if maintainers decide operational-notice routing should remain hard-coded or plugin-owned rather than a core config contract.

recommendation.title: Require Security/Product Review Before Merge
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but require the shrinkwrap to be removed or explicitly authorized, the branch rebased, the config/API contract approved, and real affected-channel proof added before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This option spans security-owned dependency policy, public config direction, and merge gating, and the recent GitHub metadata shows steipete merging adjacent security/delivery work.
